description: Unique id: the source's own id where it has one, with a source prefix (wahis-7918, empres-i-UNFAO-..., adis-<week>-<country>-<disease>, govuk-ai-<case ref>, govuk-bt-<season>-<area>, ie-dafm-bt-..., fi-ruokavirasto-asf-...).
event: a WOAH or FAO event; case: one confirmed case from a national page; aggregate: a published total for an area or week.
Who published the figure.
Where to check the figure. For WAHIS, the event's page.
When the source last updated the record or page, as the source gives it.
When OutbreakLens read the source.
One of: bird-flu, bluetongue, asf, fmd, sheep-goat-pox, lsd, newcastle-disease, other.
Disease as the source names it, shortened (WAHIS's '(Inf. with)' removed).
Serotype, subtype or strain where given.
Country code. Kosovo uses XKX.
Country name in GOV.UK style.
First-level area: UK nation, Irish county, Finnish region, or the Natural Earth region elsewhere.
Second-level area where the record is placed there: UK county or council area, Finnish municipality.
The place exactly as the source publishes it, at settlement level at most. Blank where the source gives only points or premises detail.
The level of lat and lon.
Latitude of the centre of the area at place_level, 2 decimal places. Never a premises.
Longitude of the centre of the area at place_level, 2 decimal places. Never a premises.
Species affected, joined with '; '.
Kept animals, wild animals or both. Blank when the source does not say.
Event or outbreak start. For aggregates, the start of the period counted.
Date of confirmation where given.
Latest report date. For aggregates, the date the counts run to.
Outbreaks or affected premises, herds or epidemiological units. WAHIS: all outbreaks in the event's latest report. GOV.UK bluetongue: confirmed cases (premises). DAFM: herd cases.
Animals affected, where given. WAHIS: cumulative cases in the latest report. Ruokavirasto: wild boar.
Animal deaths, where given.
Event status as the source gives it.
Context: report type, reason, how the place was set, caveats.
Ids of rows from other sources that describe the same event, joined with '; ' (up to 20, then '+N more'). Rows are never merged.
